lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs' season has reached the point where a three-goal lead feels less like security than a countdown. Thursday's 4-3 loss to the Kings - Toronto's eighth straight defeat - prompted a canceled practice and a meeting with Rory McIlroy and sports psychologist Bob Rotella. That is a striking intervention for a hockey club sitting 8-13, 13th in the Eastern Conference, with 19 points and 13 games separating it from the pace ahead. Jim Hiller is under the microscope, and rightly so; the collapse against Los Angeles was not bad luck, but another failure to close. No injury update changes the central story: the team's confidence is wounded, and its response must come from its core. McIlroy's message was joy. Tonight, against Columbus, sentiment expires. The Blue Jackets visit at 7 p.m. ET on Sportsnet, and Toronto must stop the eight-game skid before this season becomes a salvage job.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The offseason began with a clean cut, not a ceremonial farewell. Toronto non-tendered Davis Schneider on Friday, making the fan favourite a free agent and reducing the 40-man roster to 39. That decision stings because Schneider once looked like the sort of homegrown spark a lineup could build around; now, after a season split between Toronto and Buffalo, the Jays have decided the opportunity cost is greater than the nostalgia. His departure creates space, but space is not improvement. Toronto needs an outfielder who can claim regular at-bats, more dependable offense, and a roster plan sturdy enough to survive another winter of patchwork. The final record was -2.0 points, but that is background now, not a battle cry. Watch what fills Schneider's vacated spot: the next addition must raise the lineup's ceiling, not merely occupy a chair.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors beat the Pistons 105-102, moving to 6-10 on the season. They sit 4th in atlantic division, and the standings race sharpens a little every night. Before that, the club lost to the Wizards 99-103. There is runway left in the schedule, and the work on rotations and matchups matters as much as the scoreboard. Next up: vs. Bucks on Mon 11/23 at 7:30 PM ET. Around the NBA, the offseason machinery is already whirring - front offices are mapping out draft boards, free-agent target lists are being quietly circulated, and cap projections are being stress-tested against every conceivable scenario. For the Toronto Raptors, the conversation centers on which direction the rebuild takes next and whether the draft lottery delivers the kind of franchise-altering talent that can accelerate the timeline.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: A one-game winning streak has steadied Washington's footing, but not erased the wobble. At 3-5-1, the Commanders sit second in the NFC East, two games behind, and Monday night offers a chance to turn respectable positioning into a serious climb. Rachaad White's late addition to the injury report, limited Friday with a heel injury, is the immediate concern. His availability matters because Jacory Croskey-Merritt is only working his way back from a groin injury, leaving Austin Ekeler as the likely insurance policy in a backfield that cannot afford to lose its balance. The emotional edge belongs to Jonathan Allen, returning to Washington with the feelings from his departure still fresh. This is no reunion tour; it is a measuring stick. Watch Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET against Cincinnati: the Commanders must protect their quarterback, win the ground game, and prove the recent surge is more than a pause between setbacks.

article.title: Raptors Beat Pistons as Barnes Scores 29
paragraphs: The Raptors beat the Pistons 105-102 last night, with Scottie Barnes scoring 29 points, Allen Graves grabbing 10 rebounds and Immanuel Quickley handing out 10 assists. Toronto visits the Bucks on Monday at 7:30 PM ET. The Leafs host the Blue Jackets tonight at 7:00 PM on Sportsnet, with Anthony Stolarz projected to start against Cam Talbot. Toronto has lost eight straight and will look for a lift after meeting Rory McIlroy and his sports psychologist.

The Jays have cut Davis Schneider, creating room for future additions before their regular-season opener at the Yankees on March 25 at 1:35 PM ET. The Commanders face the Bengals on Monday at 8:15 PM on ESPN, while running back Rachaad White is limited with a heel injury. Toronto's next baseball game is 124 days away.
